description: Displayed opposite the entrance to Base Aérea La Aurora since the late 1970s; the longest-standing of the four airframes on this street. Guatemala was the last military operator of the Mustang. Identity is genuinely unresolved: AirHistory states the aircraft was first displayed in camouflage wearing "360" and was repainted overall silver in the mid-1980s wearing what it calls the FAKE serial "336"; the Warbird Registry entry (compiled with Tulio Soto and Mario E. Overall) instead says FAG 336 was delivered March 1956 and displayed at La Aurora "as FAG 360; 1979-1987". Construction number and USAAF serial unknown from every source consulted. tail_number therefore left blank rather than guessed. Since 2011 it has carried a red lightning flash on the nose believed to replicate markings worn by the original 336 c.1959. Photographed in place at MGGT on 21 Nov 2020 (JetPhotos 9956387).
aliases: 336; 360; FAG 336; FAG 360; P51D; P-51D; Mustang; P51

description: On display outside the entrance to La Aurora Air Base since 2010 per AirHistory caption. Ex-USAF 69-6404; 69- is the fiscal-year order prefix and is NOT a construction year; so year_built is left blank. relato.gt (2019) confirms an A-37B standing on 11 calle / 15 avenida zona 13 alongside the Arava; the Mustang and the Huey II; which is almost certainly this airframe.
museum_name: Monumentos Aéreos de la Fuerza Aérea Guatemalteca

description: Unveiled as a monument on 1 Dec 2019 at 11 calle y 15 avenida; zona 13; with President Jimmy Morales and Israeli deputy ambassador Naama Levy present; the project was pushed by deputy Fernando Linares-Beltranena after he saw the FAG's stored airframes. Guatemala bought 11 Aravas in 1973; the type flew relief missions after the 1976 earthquake and counter-insurgency work in the 1980s; and had been grounded roughly ten years before this airframe was plinthed. Prepared for display by sanding sharp fuselage edges; repainting and stripping the navigation equipment; leaving the original seats. relato.gt notes an earlier Arava had already been installed in 2016 — if a second Arava monument exists it is not confirmed here. No serial published in either Guatemalan source; so tail_number is blank.
museum_name: Monumentos Aéreos de la Fuerza Aérea Guatemalteca

description: Listed by relato.gt (Nov 2019) as one of the four airframes on this street; described as a "Huey II" — the Huey II is a re-manufactured UH-1H; so the base airframe is a UH-1H. No serial published. Not independently photographed in this location by any source I could reach; so this is the weakest of the four entries at this site.
aliases: UH1H; UH-1; UH1; Huey; Huey II; Iroquois
